tasks.title: Persist bounded fleet intent with conditional writes
steps: Implement root and immutable paged policy/node/history/operation codecs with strict bounds.
Implement exact-request idempotency, CAS conflict and ambiguous-response reconciliation using existing storage clients.
Retain terminal operation identity; add no object-store call to business acknowledgement.
Implement Finalizing, digest-addressed candidate receipts and terminal operation-index CAS; orphan receipts grant no completion.
acceptance: No unconditional root updates or listing-based trust.
Concurrent catalog recovery is deterministic and bounded; exact RustFS semantics remain a FO-10 deployment gate.
stop_conditions: Stop on any violated safety invariant; preserve failed and ambiguous outcomes.
Reject unbounded work, incomplete inventory claims and performance results without matched workload evidence.

test_cases.name: fleet_root_unreferenced_receipt

steps: Persist per-group permit sequence and payload with repair state, snapshots and archive membership metadata.
Guard managed begin, advance, activation and manual membership paths; reject mixed unguarded participants.
Commit cancellation fences before releasing unused permits; retain blocked reservations without quorum.
acceptance: Zero late membership actions after a terminal cancellation fence.
All existing group membership and snapshot regressions pass.
stop_conditions: Stop on any violated safety invariant; preserve failed and ambiguous outcomes.
Reject unbounded work, incomplete inventory claims and performance results without matched workload evidence.

test_cases.name: fleet_permit_crash_recovery

test_cases.name: fleet_permit_joint_cancel

test_cases.name: fleet_permit_snapshot_roundtrip
test_cases.oracle: Snapshot and archive restore preserve consumed sequence and active permit; old payloads cannot replay.

test_cases.name: fleet_permit_quorumless_fence

test_cases.name: fleet_permit_no_manual_bypass

test_cases.name: fleet_permit_legacy_startup_cannot_seed_managed_history

tasks.title: Enroll trusted nodes and every managed cell history
steps: Add CAS-authorized node-set revisions with bounded route and permission refresh.
Expose domain-owned dynamic dormant history registration with schema and inventory checks.
Enroll all births and initial placements before activation; block incomplete imports and retired-slot reuse.
Fence cancelled births using conditional tombstones at the existing per-cell-name birth key; preserve the name and incarnation permanently in v1.
Support an empty managed host and node-level readiness without eager per-history registration; separate placement/leadership exclusion from evacuation.

Confirm permanent namespace group-identity claims before birth admission; atomically index group identity and cell name, retain harmless pre-admission claims after cancellation and refuse earlier fleet-root protocols.

Maintain an authoritative bounded namespace birth-intent inventory before publication; freeze admissions by root CAS and reconcile every pending decision. Frozen birth inventory alone does not certify complete import, membership quiescence or removal.

Observe enrolled group configuration through a new quorum ReadIndex per invocation, without requiring a SQL image. Preserve joint roles, exact birth/process identity, bounded reply retention and original-deadline cancellation; this is not a complete-import or removal certificate.

Implement rooted per-namespace import Preparing/Inventory/Coverage/Handoff/Complete phases over the exact frozen set, conditional pending-decision cancellation, retained stop/resume and exact stored-candidate replay after lost replies.

Verify every live group through opaque safe-ReadIndex observations, complete retained witness/history/member-claim reads, and unresolved-admission refusal before exact catalog-scoped namespace handoff. This does not certify fleet-wide compiled namespace coverage or node absence.

Bind committed group guards and permits to the exact catalog fingerprint. Store managed ownership in each new canonical birth so an adopted immutable-unmanaged namespace can initialize later births with guards in the first sync while old histories replay their committed enrollment.

Root an append-only paged namespace/class registry before managed host startup, history/import admission and new managed birth reservation. Pin schema and physical data-root identity; preserve every earlier declaration when adding capacity.

Check all rooted namespace declarations against exact catalog handles, original retained import coverage, current canonical admission indexes and every fleet history. Include unpublished/reserved/cancelled births and offline histories; this bounded read is not a capacity or removal receipt.

Qualify actual managed retirement through peer seed/joint membership, outgoing-voter shutdown and fresh-quorum completion; reopen the stale intact engine and refuse metadata/engine rebinding under a fresh member ID. Abort the unusable learner and verify a newer member on a distinct engine through archive seed and native writes. Fresh learner admission must refresh current rooted host/history authorization within the original seed deadline and metadata budget rather than using startup eligibility.

Stamp opaque membership authorizations with their rooted minimum trust revision. On managed hosts, gate only fresh repair starts on actual source/target process acknowledgements through the existing authenticated metadata RPC; retain exact committed-plan continuation, original deadlines, memory bounds, cancellation, drain and joined shutdown. Bucket pins, published views and correctly authenticated unsolicited frames do not create node trust or local group state.

Bind complete trust cuts, successor checks and authenticated node metadata routes to the exact catalog fingerprint. Refuse cross-catalog acknowledgements even with the same fleet ID, physical pins, epochs and revision numbers. Hard-cut the experimental protocol with mandatory catalog-scoped routes and marker 1; retain no compatibility reader.

Qualify complete process and node-set revocation over real blocked TLS connections. Resume an already seeded learner on the same engine under a new process during restart exclusion; require all original peers to install its new view, old sockets to close, old publishers to refuse revival, verified SQL catch-up and joint completion. Preserve pending transport through exclusion modes, then require final Removed to cancel and join it before a valid late advisory publication is refused.

While a successor repair is accepted but not yet applied, retain its waiter through the previous terminal repair status. Refuse a conflicting result only after the accepted position applies; a prior Complete/Aborted plan does not prove the new proposal failed. Preserve exact quorum reconciliation of ambiguous outcomes.

Persist explicit Nodes or PhysicalHosts replica separation in the fleet head and initial genesis pin. Default to PhysicalHosts. Fresh managed births and actual fresh repair admission enforce the selected rooted contract; exact committed repairs remain continuable after exclusion. Node-only colocation grants no physical failure independence. Hard-cut prior protocol/records with marker 1 and no compatibility reader.

Admit Active-to-Draining evacuation intent through one exact root CAS after an internal complete-inventory scan. Atomically persist its canonical operation, excluded node epoch and the single disruption slot, with a retained root digest that refuses generic deletion/reset. Reconcile admitted exact retries through the journal, including after later incomplete namespace additions. This is exclusion admission only, with no shutdown, node-absence, terminal evacuation/removal, reservation release or completed-controller claim. Permanently bind each evacuation operation ID to its exact canonical request through conditional create before root CAS, even if that candidate loses. Admitted reads and retry reconciliation verify that immutable binding; missing request bytes refuse.

Prepare bounded digest-addressed evacuation candidates by consuming complete rooted inventory and owning actual authenticated RF3 observations plus exact physical archive replay. Retain one fixed publication cut per pending history across writes and replay retries; check stable membership, exact settled latest permits, current rooted node/disk/process/engine bindings and failure-domain separation. Reserved births block; canonical cancellations remain explicit. Recheck rooted inputs around immutable paged receipt work. Candidates leave the root and disruption slot unchanged; fresh terminal health, physical joins/fences and the atomic terminal receipt remain required.

Order every managed boot, including intact restart, against Finalizing through a permanent exact boot request and root CAS before endpoint publication. Bind trust and running-host authorization to the original boot process. Consume a complete historical candidate through fresh inventory and an owned process probe, then atomically root the Finalizing projection and higher node epoch while retaining the disruption slot. Reconcile exact committed retries without live inputs; preserve deadline checks at CAS. This boot fence grants no physical stop, terminal removal or resource release; Terminal integration is completed by the verification and removal step below.

Pin the closure verification key at rooted boot and fsync an exact boot/process/engine lifecycle guard before endpoint publication. Admit scoped stop/fence work through the Node-owned bounded task and real engine worker with original deadlines. Sign immutable bounded closure only after actual Node/engine owners join; reconcile lost publication replies. Keep local acceptance, physical closure and future terminal removal/slot release distinct. Physical closure alone retains the disruption slot; terminal completion is a separate verified CAS.

Expose exact stop/fence work over authenticated, purpose-separated Raft control with rooted node routes, both boot/process/engine identities and body-digest binding. Recheck current origin boot for new receiver admissions. Preserve the original origin budget and the TLS-admission receiver deadline through header/body reading, bounded queueing and engine sync. Lost callers/transport replies remain unconfirmed and do not cancel receiver-owned admitted work. Both endpoints may be empty; no Actor lease or dummy cell is required. Compose a real voter replacement, concurrent survivor writes, scoped stop and signed joined closure; Terminal CAS and slot release require the separate runtime verification step below.

Admit Ready/Active capacity through an owned complete-inventory scan, authenticated exact-boot probe and one request-journaled root CAS. Record explicit deployment attestation separately from installed startup bounds; refuse profile-version rebinding, stale boots, unfit limits and concurrent exclusion. Current opaque capacity authorization requires the exact rooted epoch/boot and journal; historical acceptance and raw Active metadata supply no new placement reservation. Fresh occupancy and resource/movement reservations remain the planner boundary; measured platform probes and operator workflows remain pending.

Resume verification from rooted Finalizing without rebinding stop authority. Own fresh quorum/archive proofs, renew every live group after replay and recheck survivor processes, inventory, settled permits and bounded proof age. Verify exact joined-owner signed closure, then atomically publish the receipt, tombstone the node and release its disruption slot. Reconcile exact retries through the permanent journal; incomplete imports, failed survivors and unconfirmed closure retain the slot. Resource release, unreachable-owner isolation and the owned fleet controller belong to later packages.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_unknown_node
test_cases.oracle: An actual valid bucket storage pin/process view cannot enroll an unrooted node. Authenticated native node-metadata requests and unsolicited Control/Data frames for unknown or dormant histories refuse before body admission, leaving rooted node entries, engine groups, dormant metadata and application callbacks unchanged. Directory discovery uses exact rooted entries without listing.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_route_revocation
test_cases.oracle: Compose the actual source/target trust-acknowledgement scenario with a seeded learner restart on the same engine and new process. Superseded blocked metadata and consensus/data connections close without stopping the live fleet; old publication cannot replace the new view, verified native SQL catches up, and joint promotion completes. An empty peer keeps a blocked call through RestartPending/ResizePending/Draining/Evacuated; Removed cancels and joins physical I/O, releases metadata reservations, and refuses a valid late directory republication. All owning SDK nodes are joined. Privileged lifecycle fixture edits are not an operator evacuation/removal certificate.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_birth_drain_race
test_cases.oracle: A birth racing drain is either admitted and inventoried or excluded from the node. Actual empty hosts finish the admitted original voters through registration, quorum/archive writes and retained references after drain/restart/resize exclusion; the opposite root-CAS ordering creates no birth or local voter.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_retired_binding
test_cases.oracle: A quorum-retired local binding cannot register or bootstrap under a fresh member ID, including an intact engine stopped in joint state before final removal and reopened without a cell registration. Its old ledger and physical slot remain retained; failed learner IDs stay consumed. A different enrolled engine registers, seeds through the managed archive path and serves verified native SQL writes. Registered-to-Active admission needs no restart; startup Active cannot bypass current Draining exclusion. Catalog lifecycle edits in this native fixture grant no evacuation/removal certificate.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_incomplete_import
test_cases.oracle: Missing history enrollment blocks removal certification even when reachable-node scans look empty.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_dynamic_bounds
test_cases.oracle: Dynamic registration and initialization obey metadata, group and body budgets under cancellation.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_empty_host
test_cases.oracle: A node with zero groups can prove bounded readiness and install namespace/class trust without a dummy business cell.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_physical_host
test_cases.oracle: Default PhysicalHosts policy refuses a real colocated learner after actual participant trust acknowledgements, without consuming membership or releasing its root reservation. Fence the unused permit, then seed/promote a distinct-host replacement and verify native S3 SQL. Explicit Nodes policy permits actual colocated RF3 birth and repair, without claiming physical-host failure independence.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_eligibility_modes
test_cases.oracle: Restart and resize target exclusions are distinct from full-evacuation intent in authenticated inspection.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_cancelled_birth
test_cases.oracle: An immutable cancellation at the exact name key defeats a held late birth, all later incarnations and a different cancellation payload without overwriting the winner.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_birth_wins_delayed_cancellation
test_cases.oracle: A cancellation losing the exact-name create returns the live birth and cannot revoke its members or claim deletion.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_cancelled_birth_lost_reply
test_cases.oracle: Lost tombstone replies reconcile by exact reads; lost confirmation remains explicitly ambiguous and a fresh adapter finds the same immutable result.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_birth_cancellation_deadline
test_cases.oracle: The original cancellation deadline drops its physical waiter and preserves uncertainty until an exact-key winner is reconciled; no detached writer or absence-based release.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_invalid_birth_tombstone
test_cases.oracle: Malformed or non-current cancellation identities refuse birth observation/creation instead of treating a tombstone as missing.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_empty_host_local_controls
test_cases.oracle: An enrolled zero-cell host reports actual empty physical inventory, pins storage despite a lost successful CAS reply, bounds unpolled controls and completes owned handoff shutdown without a dummy cell; local observation is not remote capacity readiness.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_stale_host_authorization
test_cases.oracle: Saved host authorization is refused with a typed catalog conflict after the rooted registration disappears; unrelated startup failures cannot satisfy the test.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_node_registration_retry
test_cases.oracle: Exact registration retries reconcile after later roots and lost replies; changed payload and duplicate durable disk are refused.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_host_capability_mismatch
test_cases.oracle: A compiled declaration digest mismatch refuses startup for that explicit reason before cell work.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_empty_engine_resume
test_cases.oracle: An empty retained engine resumes with a new process, identical storage instance and unchanged rooted pin without creating group history.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_replacement_engine_refused
test_cases.oracle: A fresh engine claiming the old node/disk is refused by the fleet pin even through a separately initialized namespace catalog prefix.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_dynamic_cancelled_read
test_cases.oracle: A held metadata read retains one bounded work reservation; a second registration is overloaded, cancellation drops the read and prevents late publication, and exact retry succeeds.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_dynamic_occupied_slot
test_cases.oracle: An unattached physical engine history remains charged and cannot be reset through dynamic registration despite spare aggregate slots.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_dynamic_stale_history
test_cases.oracle: A saved group capability whose rooted history record disappeared cannot publish dormant metadata.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_dynamic_undeclared_class
test_cases.oracle: A rooted group capability cannot select an undeclared compiled class or cause application execution.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_dynamic_close_joins_read
test_cases.oracle: Host close cancels and joins a held registration read; its physical metadata reservation releases while the unpolled waiter retains its bounded request charge until consumed.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_dynamic_trust_refresh
test_cases.oracle: An empty managed host acknowledges a newer complete rooted node cut without changing its startup observation or creating a group; shutdown joins discovery and releases metadata ownership.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_dynamic_trust_isolation
test_cases.oracle: A held background root read cannot take the foreground history-admission turn; registration still succeeds, and shutdown joins the held read before releasing its physical metadata reservation.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_node_probe_shutdown
test_cases.oracle: A resumed enrolled process accepts TLS but never replies; host shutdown joins the physical node probe and releases its reservations while the unpolled caller retains only its request permit until consumption.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_node_probe_resource_floor
test_cases.oracle: An undersized managed control budget refuses startup before storage pinning; the exact supported floor serves a node probe while both catalog readers are held and joins their physical reads on shutdown.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_node_probe_retained_age
test_cases.oracle: A caller that retains an unpolled probe cannot receive a falsely fresh observation; reported origin age includes the complete delay through SDK delivery.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_managed_gate
test_cases.oracle: Managed immutable roots refuse ordinary creation/cancellation and another catalog key scope; only a confirmed exact birth can mint enrollment authority.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_drain_race
test_cases.oracle: An admitted delayed birth remains inventoried after drain; a held admission CAS loses to a concurrent drain and cannot mint authority. This adapter case does not certify full evacuation.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_lost_reply
test_cases.oracle: A fresh adapter reconciles a lost admission response after a later drain revision; changing its admitted payload is refused.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_cancelled_writer
test_cases.oracle: Cancellation defeats a held admitted birth; its history/name remain retained and cannot authorize membership or name reuse.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_domains
test_cases.oracle: Initial RF3 birth admission rejects repeated declared physical hosts before creating a birth. This does not qualify later movement placement.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_admission_bounds
test_cases.oracle: Invalid request bounds/deadlines, unknown nodes and ineligible registered nodes cannot admit an initial placement.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_timeout_retains_intent
test_cases.oracle: An expired physical birth attempt leaves its rooted reservation intact and retry resolves that same history.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_dynamic_birth_digest
test_cases.oracle: A changed rooted birth digest under the same history binding cannot register dormant metadata against the actual immutable birth.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_corrupt_confirmation
test_cases.oracle: Corrupt immutable birth bytes remain a typed corruption error; no confirmation or reservation release occurs.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_unguarded_genesis
test_cases.oracle: Ordinary bootstrap refuses fresh and bare managed genesis without creating a member claim or attaching a voter.

test_cases.name: fleet_genesis_dynamic_replication_and_restart
test_cases.oracle: Three empty managed hosts register and initialize original voters, acknowledge an archived write and retain guard/data across restart with only self-address hints. Initialization retries through startup-recovered handles return the same guard without resetting data.

test_cases.name: fleet_genesis_startup_bootstrap
test_cases.oracle: Confirmed fresh births initialize their original voters during managed startup with enrollment present before attachment.

test_cases.name: fleet_genesis_waiter_cancel_and_retry
test_cases.oracle: While the permanent claim is held, synced genesis is parked and counted once; dropping the caller does not orphan the submitted initializer, and same-capability retry returns the existing guard.

test_cases.name: fleet_genesis_shutdown_during_claim
test_cases.oracle: Host close cancels the held claim and joins the initializer while retaining the caller permit; retained guarded state resumes without a new identity.

test_cases.name: fleet_genesis_stale_history_refused
test_cases.oracle: A saved birth capability cannot initialize a voter after its rooted history is withdrawn; no local group is created.

test_cases.name: fleet_genesis_foreign_namespace_owner_refused
test_cases.oracle: A matching declared capability digest cannot authorize a namespace owned by another coordination key scope, even with the same fleet incarnation.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_group_identity
test_cases.oracle: A group ID cannot be rooted under two names, incarnations or namespace/data prefixes; a conflict changes neither root revision nor inventory.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_external_group_conflict
test_cases.oracle: An existing unmanaged namespace identity claim refuses new managed birth admission before any fleet history or birth is published, preserving the foreign decision.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_group_claim_cancellation
test_cases.oracle: A confirmed pre-CAS identity claim fences a competing namespace; cancellation leaves no birth or group authorization, and the original request can resume without releasing or resetting the claim.

test_cases.name: fleet_birth_reservation_group_claim_lost_reply
test_cases.oracle: A lost identity-claim confirmation can leave only the permanent claim; exact retry converges and the original root request reconciles after birth confirmation and adapter recreation.

test_cases.name: namespace_birth_inventory_freeze_pending
test_cases.oracle: A held birth is in the frozen admission set; new names and mismatched-incarnation cancellation refuse while the admitted canonical writer can finish. Frozen operation retries preserve the same root and never list.

test_cases.name: namespace_birth_inventory_freeze_wins_admission
test_cases.oracle: Freeze wins the CAS before a held admission: the late admission cannot create a birth, even though harmless identity/pages were prepared.

test_cases.name: namespace_birth_inventory_pending_cancel_fence
test_cases.oracle: A pending intent enumerated from the frozen set can be conditionally cancelled; its delayed writer cannot overwrite the exact tombstone or change the frozen inventory.

test_cases.name: namespace_birth_inventory_lost_freeze_reply
test_cases.oracle: A lost post-CAS confirmation remains ambiguous; a fresh adapter resumes the exact frozen operation without another mutation.

test_cases.name: namespace_birth_inventory_missing_state
test_cases.oracle: Missing head, pin, both, intent, index page or an occupied namespace root refuses new authority and cannot be repaired by silently recreating an empty inventory.

test_cases.name: namespace_birth_inventory_paging_and_bounds
test_cases.oracle: A 140-birth frozen set streams under 1-KiB logical record limits and bounded 64-KiB index pages, with strict page/cursor bounds and no listing or omitted/duplicate entries.

test_cases.name: namespace_birth_inventory_untracked_decision
test_cases.oracle: Validly framed bucket birth/identity objects outside the authoritative frozen inventory cannot mint GroupBirth authority or appear as enrolled histories.

test_cases.name: fleet_observation_without_image
test_cases.oracle: Leader and follower observations cover a fresh quorum barrier and coherent durable membership without a SQL image, application callback or query-reader pin; a later observation covers an acknowledged write.

test_cases.name: fleet_observation_requires_enrollment
test_cases.oracle: An unenrolled group and a rooted authorization for a different actual birth cannot mint an enrolled quorum observation; committing enrollment permits a matching fresh read.

test_cases.name: fleet_observation_partition_and_recovery
test_cases.oracle: A saved successful observation and cached local guard cannot satisfy new isolated invocations. A majority successor and the healed old process obtain new barriers covering an acknowledged successor write.

test_cases.name: fleet_observation_permit_phases
test_cases.oracle: Fresh observations retain seeding bindings, both joint voter sets and terminal membership at the corresponding durable revisions; the guard and application state survive movement.

test_cases.name: fleet_observation_cancellation_pressure_and_close
test_cases.oracle: Administrative reservations remain bounded under unpolled and overloaded calls. Dropped quorumless waiters and joined shutdown release pending reads and response reservations without minting success.

test_cases.name: namespace_import_live_cut_and_handoff
test_cases.oracle: A real live group continues quorum/archive writes while its exact frozen birth cut is inventoried and guarded. Missing proof blocks progress; Handoff refuses cancellation and only confirmed terminal ownership closes legacy new-name admission.

test_cases.name: namespace_import_pending_stop_resume
test_cases.oracle: The rooted cursor includes a held unpublished birth. Stop retains its references; explicit resume conditionally cancels it, a delayed live writer cannot overwrite the tombstone, and all canonical histories remain indexed.

test_cases.name: namespace_import_claim_stop_race
test_cases.oracle: A stopped root wins while another adapter holds namespace-claim CAS. The late claim may settle but its stale root CAS cannot advance stopped progress; exact resume reconciles the retained owner/cut.

test_cases.name: namespace_import_lost_reply_reopen
test_cases.oracle: Lost root and namespace replies across begin, claim, coverage, adoption and terminal root CAS converge after adapter recreation using the original stored request, without reconstructing the opaque group proof or reopening unmanaged births.

test_cases.name: namespace_import_catalog_scope
test_cases.oracle: Two catalogs with the same fleet incarnation have distinct binding keys. Cached foreign-scope enrollment, observations and membership permits cannot mutate a real enrolled group; a competing import cannot replace namespace ownership.

test_cases.name: namespace_import_missing_coverage_page
test_cases.oracle: A missing retained coverage page refuses handoff before ownership changes. Exact metadata restoration resumes the original rooted cut without resetting or declaring an empty set. The fleet-wide inventory check also rereads retained coverage after import completion and refuses missing metadata.

test_cases.name: namespace_import_radix_completeness
test_cases.oracle: A live quorum group and 140 cancelled births cross radix leaf boundaries; both rooted passes cover all 141 intents once, retain every history and use no object listing.

test_cases.name: fleet_genesis_imported_namespace
test_cases.oracle: Three actual managed hosts import an empty immutable-unmanaged namespace, admit a later managed birth, initialize its guard in first sync, serve native SQL writes and recover intact after physical restart.

test_cases.name: namespace_import_engine_pin_conflict
test_cases.oracle: A rooted but incorrect engine instance cannot satisfy import coverage: the actual namespace storage pin and permanent member claim must match each current voter. Failure retains frozen progress and refuses ownership handoff.

test_cases.name: fleet_inventory_namespace_coverage
test_cases.oracle: A second declared namespace invalidates a formerly complete caller-selected subset. Missing or incomplete import blocks inventory success; complete empty import restores full coverage without replacing serving Raft authority.

test_cases.name: fleet_inventory_registry_retries_and_scope
test_cases.oracle: Lost registry-CAS replies reconcile after later declarations and adapter recreation using the original candidate; changed payloads and namespace root/class replacement are refused.

test_cases.name: fleet_inventory_retains_offline_and_missing_births
test_cases.oracle: Offline endpoints do not remove histories. Full inventory retains live/cancelled canonical intents; missing immutable decisions refuse success until exact metadata restoration.

test_cases.name: fleet_inventory_namespace_bound
test_cases.oracle: The 64-namespace bound refuses a 65th declaration without changing the root; existing namespace identity cannot be replaced at the bound.

test_cases.name: fleet_registry_compiled_namespace_gate
test_cases.oracle: A valid registered capability digest cannot boot an undeclared compiled namespace. Failed startup binds no fleet storage pin; declaring the exact namespace permits intact-engine resume with both compiled declarations.

test_cases.name: fleet_inventory_reserved_births
test_cases.oracle: Fresh managed namespaces enumerate root reservations before intent publication and retain live/cancelled outcomes whose root confirmations are still pending; reconciliation never converts these physical references into absence proof.

test_cases.name: fleet_inventory_registry_no_reset
test_cases.oracle: The fleet head permanently retains the namespace count. Registry deletion/regression and lost index pages cannot recreate an empty registry or admit a replacement set; exact metadata restoration resumes the original declaration.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_move_trust_acknowledgements
test_cases.oracle: With one target catalog read held, a fresh managed Begin cannot consume its permit or create a learner before the actual source and target processes acknowledge the authorization revision; native SQL continues. Cancellation and expiry leave consumption unchanged. Releasing the read admits the same plan. Exact committed-plan retries and abort still work with an unreachable target and a newer rooted capability. Shutdown joins an unpolled 60-second fresh-admission waiter within the existing bound and retains its unresolved root reservation. This does not qualify complete route revocation or node removal.

test_cases.name: fleet_enrollment_catalog_scoped_node_trust
test_cases.oracle: Two actual hosts use separate coordination catalogs with the same fleet ID, shared namespace storage, identical declared capabilities and matching rooted physical records/epochs. Both install at least the requested revision. A counted TCP proxy proves the metadata RPC reached the other process; its signed response must refuse cross-catalog trust acknowledgement. Both engines and application callbacks remain unchanged. Unit checks also reject foreign-scope trust reuse/successor installation and missing/zero route scope.

test_cases.name: fleet_root_replica_separation
test_cases.oracle: Persist and reopen the selected separation policy; an incompatible initialize request conflicts. Missing pin policy/root fields and unknown separation refuse; an existing pin refuses root recreation.

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_inventory_admission
test_cases.oracle: Complete inventory, operation identity, one disruption slot and a pinned node Active-to-Draining epoch commit atomically. Authenticated observation confirms exclusion; a fresh learner admission to that node refuses without consumption. Native S3 writes continue. No stop/removal proof is granted.

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_inventory_gate
test_cases.oracle: An empty actual spare cannot bypass omitted namespaces, incomplete adopted import or a missing canonical history. No exclusion/operation is published on refusal. Completing the empty import and restoring injected history coverage allows typed exclusion admission; it does not certify removal.

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_stale_inventory_cas

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_lost_reply_and_retained_slot

Exact original retry reconciles its original revision without another epoch or new inventory obligation. Changed node/principal conflicts; another disruption remains blocked and generic slot deletion refuses. Missing canonical operation-request bytes refuse both admission inspection and further disruption, and are never treated as a free slot.

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_one_disruption_slot

No late write appears after releasing the fixture gate; exact retry freshly revalidates and admits. This controlled gate does not assert cancellation of an arbitrary remote committed PUT.

test_cases.name: fleet_peer_observation_empty_coordinator
test_cases.oracle: An empty coordinator obtains authenticated safe-ReadIndex observations from each actual RF3 member before any SQL image. Whole-call age includes retained SDK replies; later native S3 SQL is covered without creating local groups or query-reader pins.

test_cases.name: fleet_peer_observation_requires_resident_history
test_cases.oracle: Rooted history and node trust do not activate dormant target metadata or grant fresh quorum. Dormant targets and invalid revision/timeout inputs refuse with zero local groups and no application callback.

test_cases.name: fleet_peer_observation_minority_cancel_and_shutdown

test_cases.name: fleet_peer_observation_fresh_catalog_and_owned_io
test_cases.oracle: After both endpoints acknowledge a newer trust cut, an injected older catalog root cannot mint a remote quorum observation. A held actual target catalog read is cancelled on disconnect with physical IO joined, while native S3 writes continue under cached Raft authority.

test_cases.name: fleet_peer_observation_repair_roles
test_cases.oracle: A qualified exact replacement boot receives a canonical resource-backed movement permit. An empty coordinator observes actual learner bindings, joint outgoing voters and terminal RF3 through fresh quorum RPCs; real SQL remains continuous after replacement.

test_cases.name: fleet_published_cut_configuration_progress
test_cases.oracle: Actual RF3 safe observations freeze a coherent published image and applied configuration cut. Configuration-only permit fencing advances apply without user SQL, and intact full-cluster restart can relabel the same image at later positions. All survivors cover the fixed cut; later S3 writes preserve coverage without changing it. Different configuration revisions conflict.

test_cases.name: fleet_published_cut_excludes_private_sql_image
test_cases.oracle: While the real second SQL callback is held after private mutation, a remote quorum observation retains the old exact published state with no query pin or local observer replica. After release, S3 acknowledgement, physical image position and native SQL result agree. Canonical empty and missing publication remain distinct.

test_cases.name: archive_empty_configuration_roundtrip_and_lost_reply
test_cases.oracle: Publish durable cold configuration with no SQLite/payload object, reconcile a lost conditional-head reply, and retain exact empty references across later configuration progress.

test_cases.name: archive_empty_reference_survives_first_image_without_erasure
test_cases.oracle: First SQL establishes a complete snapshot; an old empty cut cannot erase newer archived data. Empty capture refuses an applied image, while exact empty restore never reclaims live images.

test_cases.name: archive_empty_and_mixed_batches_keep_each_history_verified
test_cases.oracle: Two real cold archives and a mixed cold/populated batch retain input order and independent verified state under the existing bounded publisher.

test_cases.name: native_empty_archive_seed_then_first_s3_write
test_cases.oracle: Actual RF3 source and fresh learner seed from canonical-empty S3 material with zero application callbacks or fabricated generations, then acknowledge and query the first real S3 write.

test_cases.name: native_empty_archive_seed_refuses_minority
test_cases.oracle: A reachable isolated original voter plus complete empty archive cannot seed a learner without fresh quorum, and no application callback runs.

test_cases.name: fleet_empty_archive_seed_retains_guard_and_completes_repair
test_cases.oracle: Actual managed cold RF3 repair retains the exact fleet binding/consumed permit through S3 learner activation, joint promotion and stable retirement, before the first native S3 command. Privileged capacity/permit fixture inputs do not qualify the pending controller.

test_cases.name: fleet_archive_coverage_empty_and_data
test_cases.oracle: Only exact immutable sets that physically replay may cover a fixed publication cut; canonical-empty, first SQL image, retained references and later data preserve exact history/configuration and complete prefix coverage.

test_cases.name: fleet_archive_coverage_configuration_and_replay_failure
test_cases.oracle: Valid downloaded hashes cannot substitute for physical replay; insufficient scratch capacity refuses and quarantines the verifier, and a changed membership revision refuses an earlier archive proof. Full snapshots retain original publication positions; intact restart aliases remain covered without replaying a callback.

test_cases.name: fleet_archive_coverage_selected_reference_and_deadline
test_cases.oracle: The original deadline suppresses proof through held payload IO or delayed polling; a missing selected manifest never falls back to a healthy newer head.

test_cases.name: archive_preserves_publication_origin_across_protocol_progress
test_cases.oracle: An actual producer held across protocol-only progress retains its exact earlier publication position in immutable manifests, and a recovered alias is preserved independently of the archive applied cut; both sets physically replay the native SQL value.

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_candidate_complete_inventory
test_cases.oracle: Own real authenticated RF3 observations and exact physical canonical-empty replay while walking every rooted history. Repeated candidate publication is digest-stable, leaves root and exclusion unchanged, retains the active disruption slot, and permits subsequent S3 business writes.

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_candidate_replay_failure_and_root_change
test_cases.oracle: Failed selected archive payload reads keep the exact history pending and grant no candidate. Retry physically verifies populated SQL. A changed rooted permit invalidates the old candidate and fresh preparation refuses a still-unconsumed latest permit.

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_candidate_reserved_cancelled_and_missing_import
test_cases.oracle: Reserved births cannot be skipped or recorded as cancelled. Immutable cancellation plus rooted reconciliation invalidates the old attempt; a fresh walk consumes both live and cancelled histories. A newly declared incomplete namespace invalidates candidates and refuses fresh verification even when its catalog handle is supplied.

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_candidate_fixed_cut_under_writes
test_cases.oracle: Freeze a real RF3 canonical-empty publication once, continue S3-acknowledged SQL writes, and physically verify a later exact archive against the retained old cut without moving the business boundary. Candidate publication and further writes both succeed. Unrelated rooted Operations progress preserves the same candidate; deleting the active canonical operation refuses publication even though the placement and permit basis is unchanged.

test_cases.name: fleet_evacuation_candidate_after_voter_replacement
test_cases.oracle: Perform real guarded S3 learner seeding, joint promotion/removal and stable RF3 completion. Evacuation candidate verification consumes the new dynamically joined member binding and latest completed permit while the departed original voter retains physical history. Subsequent S3 writes and queries succeed on the three survivors. Consume the candidate through rooted Finalizing and stop the actual retired voter over authenticated Raft control while survivor S3 writes continue. Join its Node without another shutdown command, require retained physical group history in the close report, verify its signed closure, and perform another survivor write. Recreate the controller in Finalizing, re-establish the same fixed business cut from fresh quorum responses, physically replay its archive, atomically certify removal and release the slot, reconcile the retained receipt, admit the next disruption and verify another successful business write.

test_cases.name: fleet_boot_epoch_survives_node_state_changes
test_cases.oracle: Actual managed hosts retain the exact boot claim through Active and Draining epoch changes. Canonical node decoding and authenticated current-enrollment observations succeed without rewriting the nested original boot epoch.

test_cases.name: fleet_finalization_boot_fence_and_retry
test_cases.oracle: Missing inventory refuses before admission. A fresh process probe and one CAS bind the exact candidate, physical process and new Finalizing epoch. Lost responses and reopened-adapter retries confirm the original journal without live inputs; changed request payloads refuse, another disruption remains blocked and S3 business writes continue.

test_cases.name: fleet_finalization_blocks_intact_boot
test_cases.oracle: After the old actual node owner joins, a real same-directory retained-engine restart with saved authorization refuses the rooted Finalizing fence. The historical epoch remains fixed and all other owners join with scratch reclaimed.

test_cases.name: fleet_finalization_new_boot_invalidates_candidate
test_cases.oracle: An actual retained-engine Draining restart claims a new process and epoch while retaining the engine. The previous candidate refuses; a freshly verified candidate may fence only the newer journal-confirmed boot.

test_cases.name: fleet_finalization_inflight_boot_wins_cas
test_cases.oracle: Hold finalization after its real process probe. A separate catalog adapter admits an actual retained-engine restart first. The held finalization CAS loses, creates no rooted Finalizing projection, and cannot rebind its permanent request identity; survivor writes and joined cleanup succeed.

test_cases.name: rooted_boot_refresh_restores_only_retained_routes
test_cases.oracle: A journal-admitted process supersession cancels old physical pools and grants. Verified new discovery recreates pools only for retained group/query obligations, refreshes logical grants without advancing membership or grant revisions, rejects the old view and creates no pool for an empty discovery or the local node.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_waiter_loss_still_joins_and_signs
test_cases.oracle: Retain an admitted local stop waiter until its own domain closes: the reply is Closed and signed closure remains unconfirmed before actual physical join. Then join, verify the exact boot-pinned signed closure and write through survivors. Separately hold the actual engine sync, discard the waiter, and observe autonomous Node.finished without a second shutdown signal. Post-join publication reconciles a lost successful PUT reply; a checksum-correct body edit cannot forge the signature. Owner/scratch cleanup succeeds.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_cancellation_fence_defeats_late_stop
test_cases.oracle: Persist and retry a local same-epoch cancellation fence. A delayed stop refuses, the real node stays live, the rooted finalization/slot remains held, and a later unplanned teardown produces no signed closure.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_closure_waits_for_physical_owner_join
test_cases.oracle: Hold the actual engine lock drop after stop acceptance. Refuse closure while physical ownership remains, refuse late fence cancellation, preserve survivor writes, then observe joined closure without another shutdown signal after releasing the gate.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_changed_inventory_refuses_admission
test_cases.oracle: Add an actual incomplete namespace after Finalizing. New stop admission refuses; a local fence may still narrow authority and raw shutdown creates no closure. This is not the required incomplete-import test at the actual terminal removal boundary.

test_cases.name: fleet_lifecycle_fences_and_boot_nonce_survive_reopen
test_cases.oracle: Use the actual engine worker and retained reopen. Fences and accepted stops survive fsync/reopen, accepted work cannot be cancelled, changed fields cannot reuse a boot nonce, a newer fresh nonce can replace the old boot even with the same process hint, and delayed old stop/foreign-catalog authority refuses.

test_cases.name: fleet_lifecycle_expired_queued_stop_has_no_effect
test_cases.oracle: Hold a prior physical sync while a stop waits in the engine queue; expire its original deadline before release and require no accepted local guard.

test_cases.name: fleet_lifecycle_failed_sync_grants_no_cached_acceptance
test_cases.oracle: Inject a real sync failure and require no cached accepted stop or closure authority; join the failed engine without asserting that ambiguous disk work did not commit.

test_cases.name: fleet_lifecycle_missing_record_refuses_resume
test_cases.oracle: Close and join the real engine, delete only its mandatory lifecycle record, fsync, then require LostStableState on Resume rather than silently creating an empty guard.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_signal_retries_are_bounded
test_cases.oracle: Flood the actual shutdown channel through the production delivery helper with 10,000 accepted retries. Exactly one signal is queued, its confirmed historical delivery survives receiver closure, and a first failed delivery remains unconfirmed. The real held-engine-lock native case also reconciles 32 exact accepted requests before physical join.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_rpc_empty_nodes_and_fence
test_cases.oracle: Use real TLS between two empty managed nodes with no business-cell scope or Actor-lease lookup. Refuse stale minimum cuts and wrong target boot nonces, sync/retry a fence and reject the delayed stop; no physical closure or slot release follows.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_rpc_waiter_loss_still_joins
test_cases.oracle: Send the real Raft-control RPC to a fault-injected actual Node. Hold engine sync, discard the origin SDK waiter, release physical work and observe Node.finished without another stop signal; the exact signed closure is verified and survivor S3 writes continue.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_rpc_expired_metadata_wait_has_no_effect
test_cases.oracle: Hold actual fleet-head reads past the original RPC budget. The response remains unconfirmed, the late worker cannot admit a stop, a subsequent fence succeeds and the target remains live.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_rpc_removed_origin_cannot_admit_work
test_cases.oracle: After authenticated empty-node discovery, remove the origin in the root. Its stop cannot admit a guard; a current surviving origin subsequently fences the same target, proving no stop won.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_mac_binds_purpose_channel_payload_and_reply
test_cases.oracle: The production Wire codec binds stop purpose, TLS exporter, payload digest, exact request tag, nonce and response. Read-only-purpose replay, other TLS channels and altered payloads/headers refuse.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_wire_requires_exact_root_and_physical_endpoints
test_cases.oracle: Require nonzero valid boot identities and bind both origin and target to the exact catalog/fleet/node/disk/process/engine route without manufacturing a group/member identity.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_wire_rejects_unbounded_or_noncanonical_work
test_cases.oracle: Reject invalid/noncanonical nonces, missing/unknown fields, oversized bodies and timeout overflow; mismatched response digests/nonces refuse and explicit overload/conflict/unknown outcomes remain typed.

test_cases.name: fleet_stop_receiver_budget_includes_header_residence
test_cases.oracle: Anchor the receiver deadline at TLS connection admission. Header residence, clock rollback and overflow cannot renew the caller-advertised remaining budget before queueing or fsync.

test_cases.name: fleet_capacity_empty_node_qualify_and_activate
test_cases.oracle: Two actual empty managed nodes install the current trust cut. Qualify an excluded spare, activate through a fresh authenticated probe and verify current rooted capacity without a dummy cell. Reusing a profile revision with changed limits refuses; an already qualified Active process cannot change limits through this admission path.

test_cases.name: fleet_capacity_lost_reply_reconciles_after_reopen
test_cases.oracle: Lose the successful fleet-head CAS response and confirmation. Stop the target, exclude it, recreate the catalog adapter and reconcile the original historical acceptance without live inputs. Changed request payload refuses and historical acceptance cannot authorize current capacity.

test_cases.name: fleet_capacity_reboot_invalidates_authorization
test_cases.oracle: Qualify a real node and join it. An attempted intact restart reusing its process hint admits a new rooted boot nonce/key and correctly refuses directory publication; join that failed startup and refuse the old capacity and stale attestation. Preserve historical request retry. Reopen with a fresh process generation, qualify through fresh TLS and regain capacity authority; the successful reopen also proves physical ownership was released.

test_cases.name: fleet_capacity_refuses_incomplete_inventory_and_unfit_attestation
test_cases.oracle: Missing declared namespace inventory, insufficient memory/disk/slots, allowed swap, a wrong boot and mismatched running-profile digest all refuse without a node transition or root revision advance.

test_cases.name: fleet_capacity_raw_active_is_not_quantified_capacity
test_cases.oracle: Privileged fixture metadata may say Active, but a missing typed readiness record and journal link cannot mint quantified placement capacity.

test_cases.name: fleet_capacity_expired_inventory_read_cannot_activate
test_cases.oracle: Hold real fleet-head reads past the original budget. Timeout leaves no activated node or capacity authority; after releasing reads, the same unadmitted identity can qualify normally.

test_cases.name: fleet_capacity_concurrent_exclusion_defeats_activation
test_cases.oracle: Hold the actual activation head CAS after readiness verification. Another adapter excludes the node first; the held CAS loses and orphan receipt/index material grants no capacity. Actual Node owners join cleanly.

test_cases.name: fleet_removal_joined_closure_and_lost_reply
test_cases.oracle: Actual joined-owner closure is required even after fresh quorum/archive verification. Generic metadata cannot release the disruption slot. Inject loss of the successful terminal CAS response and confirmation; adapter recreation reconciles the exact historical removal without live verification or namespace handles. A changed stop request conflicts without another root revision.

test_cases.name: fleet_removal_failed_survivor_keeps_slot
test_cases.oracle: After actual quorum/archive verification and joined closure of the departing process, stop a survivor. Terminal per-group quorum renewal must refuse, preserve Finalizing and the disruption slot, and leave the remaining majority able to write. A historical positive observation cannot certify removal.

tasks.title: Plan healthy replica redistribution with reservations
steps: Implement dependency-free FleetView, FleetPolicy, projected-capacity scoring and typed refusal reasons.
Use deterministic tie breaks, cooldown/deadband and failure-domain checks.
Atomically reserve target capacity and per-node movement slots; revalidate host capacity before initialization.
Implement complete bounded assignment and final-fleet single-failure simulation; distinguish search exhaustion from infeasibility.

Use source-target gap and lexicographic pressure improvement for performance-triggered moves; explicit topology requests reduce feasible live-assignment distance while retained physical state remains charged.
Produce a complete final assignment and a legal bounded move DAG; reconcile materialization without double-crediting physical resources.

Implement boot/process/profile-scoped conservative resource accounting, monotonic attributed materialization and bounded unresolved movement debt. Preserve physical high water until a separate terminal-proof release boundary; a pure ledger grants no catalog admission authority.

Add journal-linked root-CAS resource debits using current typed capacity, owned authenticated probes and explicit deployment occupancy attestation. Preserve old-scope and unmaterialized genesis debt, refuse unknown permit attribution and prevent generic deletion/reset. Link the physical inventory producer, typed membership permit and terminal release before general fleet redistribution.

Use complete bounded authenticated physical engine inventory to attribute original voters and retained/retired slots without per-history application registration or quorum. Persist the inventory digest, reject occupied destinations and pending initialization, and preserve response memory/age through delivery and cancellation.

Atomically link exact membership intent to its target debit and active book, using owned fresh source ReadIndex and target physical inventory. Reconcile the canonical combined intent before live prerequisites; protect linked permits against generic replacement. Actual group consumption and target initialization remain mandatory.

Complete successful resource-backed moves using fresh terminal target quorum, exact physical boot of the target and every original voter that could serve a seed and durable consumed sequence, joined seed/initializer ownership and one receipt/floor/book CAS. Retain original rows and independent monotonic physical floors; exact historical retries precede live checks. Aborted, unreachable and rebooted owners remain charged. Unused reservations require the distinct quorum-fenced settlement boundary; admission or timeout never releases them.

Verify explicit complete RF3 topology proposals in the pure core. Search legal direct serial move orders under seed peaks and retained source occupancy, then complete direct restoration witnesses for each kept-node loss. Share one bounded search budget; distinguish search exhaustion, direct-path refusal and unproven restoration. Stable groups and unsettled-free fresh complete inputs are prerequisites. Automatic final assignment and owned adapter collection/execution remain separate work.

Accept distinct trusted deployment isolation for an exact boot after rooted exclusion; permanently deny restart/transport and preserve retained storage. Successful movement completion may substitute this admitted proof only for the obsolete original voter absent from fresh stable RF3. Keep full durable membership for placement/quorum while omitting quarantined endpoints from routes; retain provenance across lost replies. External platform integration remains separate work; terminal isolated-node removal is delivered under FO-07.

Settle unused movement reservations only after the exact permit is quorum-fenced on every original boot, followed by complete authenticated physical worker-exit and empty-destination proof. Atomically record a distinct fenced receipt and monotonic physical floor while releasing only the exact active book row. Preserve canonical retries across adapter recreation, lost responses and subsequent work; seeding, joint, aborted, changed-boot and unreachable owners retain debt through this path.

Settle exact Aborted permits only after all original seed owners have quorum-observed the abort and then proved physical worker exit. Distinguish retained versus empty destination history, preserve physical floors, permanent receipt identity and later reservations. Complete/Fenced/Aborted outcomes cannot be reinterpreted. Changed or unavailable boots still require their separate recovery boundary.

Generate equal-copy final assignments for the explicit keep-set in the pure core, with alternate remainder allocations, constrained direct surplus-to-deficit search, retained occupancy and one shared generation/staging/recovery budget. Return only complete verified witnesses; BalanceUnproven and SearchExhausted grant no partial authority or global infeasibility claim. Connect owned authenticated fleet collection and current guarded admission separately; weighted/load policy remains optional.

Connect the pure balanced planner to owned complete namespace, current capacity, physical binding and three-voter ReadIndex collection. Walk histories incrementally, retain genesis/retired/floor debt, refresh node inputs before planning, and describe only the first exact move for existing guarded admission and owned execution. Require terminal settlement and recollection for successors; durable fleet intent/exclusions and automatic new admission remain separate work.

Root an exact group/member/node provenance index atomically with each resource-linked permit. Resolve pruned dynamic physical bindings through the original admitted row and verified retained terminal receipt, without scans or release credit. Protect generic edits; allow lookup replacement only after a journal-confirmed unused Fenced proposal at a higher sequence on the same disk/engine.

Persist canonical desired topology, keep-set and active operation in one root CAS. Gate newly referenced birth members, resource debits and membership targets against that policy at the same CAS; preserve pre-admitted birth/permit authority and node epochs. Serialize new topology intent with node evacuation without reusing its record shape. Generic policy, operation and active-pointer edits refuse.

Consume a current opaque preview for exact operation-owned first-move admission; append its per-operation hash-radix progress index in the same CAS as debit, book, permit and binding. Resolve status and bounded pagination through canonical origin/current journals; historical retries cannot clear newer work. Complete only from a fresh exhaustive no-move preview. Cancellation first fences new admissions, settles prior effects and restores prior allowed placement without rolling back membership.
Select a required isolated-voter replacement from fresh surviving quorum, complete physical/retained occupancy and deployment bounds; preserve survivors and atomically retain selected headroom.
Account all scoped rooted reservations during required-repair selection, sharing retained-floor and unresolved-growth construction with independent final admission.
acceptance: Projected destination utilization includes every unresolved permit.
Placement-only simulations do not count as live throughput qualification.

Reject unbounded work, incomplete inventory claims and performance results without matched workload evidence.

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_five_to_six
test_cases.oracle: Equal feasible groups redistribute within deadband without co-located voters or oscillation; the symmetric reference assignment is feasible with 25 cells per six-node triple, 250 replacements and 250 copies per node, without requiring every valid planner to choose that exact assignment.

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_concurrent_targets

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_failure_domains
test_cases.oracle: Domain-shortage, temporary seed space and draining targets refuse unsafe movement.

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_unknown_load
test_cases.oracle: Incomplete or stale observations cannot count as zero utilization.

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_cooldown
test_cases.oracle: Repeated identical pressure does not reverse a completed movement inside its cooldown.

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_tied_peak_progress
test_cases.oracle: A new node receives replicas at low load despite tied source peaks and small per-cell pressure improvements.

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_retained_usage

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_search_exhaustion

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_zone_spare

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_staged_path
test_cases.oracle: A final assignment that fits but has no legal first move is refused; temporary learners and retained source state are charged at every prefix.

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_materialization_ledger
test_cases.oracle: Attributed physical samples and reservation releases cannot double-credit materialized resources; stale process samples retain conservative charges.

test_cases.name: fleet_placement_retired_destination

test_cases.name: fleet_resource_lost_reply_reconciles_and_cannot_reset_book
test_cases.oracle: Lose the successful head-CAS response and confirmation, exclude and stop the actual target, recreate the adapter and reconcile the historical debit without live inputs. Changed payload and generic book/row deletion refuse without freeing debt.

test_cases.name: fleet_resource_refuses_raw_active_and_incomplete_inputs
test_cases.oracle: The resource consumer refuses bare Active metadata, incomplete namespace inventory, a stale boot, too-small learner byte bounds and memory overcommit without advancing the root.

test_cases.name: fleet_resource_exclusion_wins_at_cas
test_cases.oracle: Hold the real resource head CAS after its owned probe; an independent adapter excludes the target first. The resource CAS loses and orphan candidate bytes grant no rooted debit or membership.

test_cases.name: fleet_resource_expired_cas_has_no_detached_writer
test_cases.oracle: Hold the actual conditional in-memory head CAS past the original operation deadline. Its owned waiter drops without a late writer; the root stays unchanged, then an exact unadmitted retry can reconcile and admit after the hold releases.

test_cases.name: fleet_resource_unmaterialized_genesis_is_not_free
test_cases.oracle: A Reserved birth and an unmaterialized Live original voter block overlapping resource admission. After actual durable initialization, authenticated inventory matches full scope/birth/member without quorum, refuses occupied-history reuse, admits another history into unused capacity, then refuses an additional debit against the actual occupied slot plus the existing reservation even when caller-attested occupied slots are zero.

test_cases.name: fleet_physical_inventory_retained_reply_and_cancellation
test_cases.oracle: An actual empty origin and target return explicit complete occupancy without a dummy cell or application callback while trust refresh reads are held. A completed unpolled reply retains its physical response charge and original age; delivery or cancellation releases that charge and transport ownership.

test_cases.name: fleet_movement_atomic_permit_drives_native_replacement
test_cases.oracle: One root CAS installs the debit, book and exact membership permit. Consume it through a real S3-seeded learner, complete joint membership and write through the new RF3. Generic deletion cannot release its unresolved resource debit.

test_cases.name: fleet_movement_lost_reply_reconciles_exact_permit
test_cases.oracle: Lose successful CAS confirmation, shut down the target and recreate the catalog adapter. Exact retry returns the original applied permit without new probes; changed membership intent conflicts.

test_cases.name: fleet_movement_minority_cannot_reserve_capacity_or_permit

test_cases.oracle: Hold one independent adapter at CAS while another reserves the final target slot for a different live group. Only the winner installs both debit and permit; the loser leaves neither projection. A fresh attempt cannot consume that occupied reservation.

test_cases.name: fleet_movement_completion_reuses_slot_preserves_floor
test_cases.oracle: Complete a real S3-seeded RF3 replacement using the original source as observer. Release its active reservation, refuse generic receipt/floor deletion, admit another history into spare capacity, retain the occupied engine slot, reconcile after a later root and execute another durable write.

test_cases.name: fleet_movement_completion_lost_reply_survives_target_shutdown
test_cases.oracle: Complete a replacement seeded by a different voter from the admission quorum source using the target as observer; lose successful CAS confirmation, physically shut down the target, recreate the adapter and reconcile the original completion before live probes. test_cases.oracle: An admitted but unstarted move cannot complete or release its last target slot. No completion receipt/root advance occurs, another debit refuses, and original RF3 writes still succeed.

test_cases.oracle: After successful RF3 replacement, physically shut down the original source. The surviving target quorum cannot substitute for that original physical owner; completion refuses without advancing the root or installing a receipt.

test_cases.name: fleet_movement_seed_waiter_loss_retains_physical_worker
test_cases.oracle: Hold actual S3 metadata I/O on a different voter from admission’s selected source, observe the source seed worker, drop the learner waiter and exceed its original deadline. test_cases.oracle: After completed RF3 replacement, physically stop a retired original voter different from the selected quorum source. Independently establish surviving target quorum; completion still refuses without root advancement because every possible seed provider must prove physical exit.

test_cases.name: fleet_movement_isolated_obsolete_repairs_three_histories

tasks.title: Expose auditable fleet operations through SDK admin and CLI
steps: Delivered keep-set begin/status/progress/wait/cancel, node add/status/qualify/activate, and graceful evacuate/prepare-removal/exact stop/remove/status through SDK, authenticated admin and CLI. Capacity and replay use explicitly configured native services. Separate lifecycle grants, canonical durable stop consent, complete replay and signed physical closure preserve authority; exact retries recover historical receipts. Intact maintenance/rejoin now has independent grants and owned execution; grace/rolling/second-failure orchestration, dry-run and resize remain unfinished. Node cancel-evacuation is delivered through the same independent fleet_cancel grant, canonical audit and exact selector validation; it returns excluded Ready and supports explicit cancellation/requalification/restart recovery.
Implement proposed operator-workflows.md commands and SDK/API phase/error contracts.
Enforce operation-specific permissions, canonical request identity, expected revisions and audit.
Provide dry-run, paginated status, wait and cancel without hidden infrastructure termination.
Expose activate, resize, guarded child stop, rolling maintenance and explicit capacity-only versus balanced completion through the same audit/permission model.

Report exact read-only quorum observation failures as typed nonterminal proof blockers, retaining the pending history and counts. Status exposes only local progress at the same root. Revalidate the root and original deadline before acknowledging waiting; never convert unknown finalization/removal mutations or storage errors into progress. CLI --wait advances acknowledged proof steps under its existing deadline and stops on unknown mutation outcomes.

Deliver maintenance prepare/cancel/status management SDK/admin/CLI adapters. Require independent fleet_maintenance preparation and fleet_cancel cancellation grants; audit before dispatch, pin catalog/node/process and canonical request identity, submit mutations once and use only read-only GET for waiting. Exact Root status never starts execution or restores health. Separate stop/return/resume management sequencing is delivered by the following step.

Expose independent stop/return/resume maintenance grants through SDK, audited admin and CLI. Stop requires fleet_stop, return fleet_maintenance, resume both fleet_maintenance and fleet_capacity. Read-only waits require actual M7, canonical M8 context and M9 plus terminal operator completion respectively; no platform provisioning or hidden mutation retry. Lost confirmation, controller recreation, cancellation refusal and correction of an unexecuted profile retain canonical identities and capacity/slot boundaries.

Management errors retain ambiguity and operator audit identity.
stop_conditions: Stop on any violated safety invariant; preserve failed and ambiguous outcomes.
